name: Tab bar
purpose: Moves between the app's top-level sections: Home, Chat and Settings. It floats at the bottom of every screen in those sections, and shows which one the user is in.

origin.notes: The iOS tab bar, UITabBar, in iOS 26's Liquid Glass style. The app draws the system's own, through BaseTabBarController, and sets only its colours: the selected tab is in text.linkSecondary. The glass is approximated with a translucent, blurred fill rather than recreated, and the icons are Material Symbols in place of SF Symbols, which may only be used on Apple's platforms. iOS 26 draws the tabs that aren't selected in the label colour, so this does too, rather than the text.secondary the app asks for. Android has its own navigation bar, which this does not draw.

inputs.content: Two to five <govuk-app-tab-bar-item> elements, one for each tab, in order. Each takes an icon attribute, the name of a Material Symbol (such as home, chat_bubble or settings); an href, to make the tab a link to another page, or name and value, to tell it apart as a button; and selected, on the tab of the section the screen is in. Its label is what is written between its tags.

icon.description: A Material Symbol, such as home, chat_bubble or settings.

href.description: Makes it a link to this page.

name.description: Without an href, makes it a button with this name, so a page listening for clicks can tell which was pressed.

value.description: Set on the button, alongside name, to say which of several it was.

selected.description: The tab of the section the screen is in.

events.name: click
events.description: From the link or button a tab draws, when it is pressed. A tab with an href goes to its page. A tab without one is a button, and pressing it selects it, as a native tab bar does; use event.target.closest('button').name to tell which was pressed and show its section.

rules: Use it only on the top-level screens of the app's sections. Hide it on screens a section pushes on top, and on modals, as the app does.
Put it last in the screen, after the content. It sticks to the bottom of the screen and the content scrolls under it.
Use the app's own tabs, in its order: Home (icon home), Chat (icon chat_bubble) and Settings (icon settings).
Select exactly one tab: the one for the section the screen is in.
Keep each label to one short word. Labels don't wrap, and are cut off if they are too long.
In a prototype of several pages, give each tab an href to its section's first page, and mark that tab selected on each of its pages.

avoid.when: On a screen that asks the user to act, such as confirm or continue
On a screen pushed on top of another, or a modal
avoid.instead: Leave it out, and give the screen a back button or a close action in its navigation bar.

avoid.when: To switch between views of the same thing

other.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Tab bars
Material Symbols, the icons it draws

references.description: Home selected, in dark mode, over the home screen
references.from: The iOS app on iOS 26, 17 November 2026

examples.name: Home selected
examples.html:
<govuk-app-tab-bar>
  <govuk-app-tab-bar-item icon="home" name="home" selected>Home</govuk-app-tab-bar-item>
  <govuk-app-tab-bar-item icon="chat_bubble" name="chat">Chat</govuk-app-tab-bar-item>
  <govuk-app-tab-bar-item icon="settings" name="settings">Settings</govuk-app-tab-bar-item>
</govuk-app-tab-bar>
